title: K Closest Points
statement:
Pick the k points of a plane that lie nearest the origin.

Contract
- `points` holds `{x, y}` integer pairs, possibly with repeats; coordinates have magnitude up to 40000. Do not modify `points` or its rows.
- Distance is straight-line (Euclidean) distance from `(0, 0)`. Compare squared distances so no square root is needed; use `long` arithmetic.
- Return a new array of exactly `k` of the input points whose distances are the `k` smallest. The order of the result does not matter.
- When several points tie for the last place, any valid choice is accepted. Throw `IllegalArgumentException` when `k < 0` or `k > points.length`; `k = 0` returns an empty array.

Examples
- `k = 2` over `(3,3) (1,-2) (-1,0) (5,1)` returns `(-1,0)` and `(1,-2)` in any order.
- A single point with `k = 1` is returned as is.
- `k` equal to the number of points returns every point.
hints: Rank points by squared distance; the square root is monotonic so it adds nothing.
Sorting everything finds the answer but does more work than needed. Keep only the best k candidates seen so far, ready to evict the worst of them.

Hold a max-heap of size k keyed by squared distance: a new point replaces the heap's farthest point when it is nearer. Intended complexity: O(n log k) time, which is O(n log n) when k grows with n as in the workload, and O(k) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: k, then the points as (x,y) pairs, for example: 2; (3,3) (1,-2) (-1,0) (5,1)
